outcomes.text: Show posture, alignment, balance, coordination, control, flexibility, mobility, strength, stamina, extension and isolation.
Perform action content: travel, turn, elevation, gesture, stillness, floor work and weight transfer.
Perform dynamic content such as fast/slow, sudden/sustained, strong/light and flowing/abrupt.
Use spatial content: pathways, levels, directions, size of movement, patterns and spatial design.
Use relationship content in duet/trio work: lead and follow, mirroring, contact, counterpoint and formations.
Show timing and rhythmic content and move in a stylistically accurate way.
Use projection, focus, spatial awareness, facial expression and phrasing to perform expressively.
In duet/trio, show musicality, sensitivity to other dancers and communicate the choreographic intent.
Show movement memory, commitment, concentration and confidence during performance.
Work safely in performance with safe execution and suitable footwear, hair and no jewellery.
Rehearse well through repetition, mental rehearsal, discipline, planning, responding to feedback and improving.
Prepare the body safely with warm-up, cool-down, nutrition and hydration.
Perform a solo of about one minute using two of the four set phrases (breathe, flux, shift, scoop).
Present the two phrases separately, to an audible 105 BPM beat, showing physical, technical, expressive and mental skills.
Perform in a duet/trio of at least three minutes with a clear choreographic intent.
Develop the other two set phrases into duet/trio material that realises the intent, without reusing solo phrases.
Show relationship content, musicality, sensitivity and safe challenging practice with a suitable aural setting.
Document the duet/trio in a programme note giving intent, phrases used and music citations.
Create a complete solo (2 to 2.5 minutes) or group dance (3 to 3.5 minutes, 2 to 5 dancers) from a set stimulus.
Include a chosen aural setting and communicate your own choreographic intention in any style.
Apply action content in choreography: travel, turn, elevation, gesture, stillness, body parts, floor work.
Apply dynamic content such as fast/slow, sudden/sustained and direct/indirect.
Apply spatial content: pathways, levels, directions, size, patterns and spatial design.
Apply relationship content: lead and follow, mirroring, accumulation, complement and contrast, contact, formations.
Use choreographic processes: researching, improvising, generating, selecting, developing, structuring and refining.
Structure a dance with forms such as binary, ternary, rondo, narrative and episodic, with unity and transitions.
Use choreographic devices: motif and development, repetition, contrast, highlights, climax, number, unison and canon.
Choose aural settings (song, instrumental, silence, found sound and more) and explain their effect on mood, structure and theme.
Know performance environments: proscenium arch, end stage, site-sensitive and in-the-round.
Communicate mood, meaning, ideas, themes and style or style fusion.
Write a 120-150 word programme note naming the stimulus, how the intent was achieved, and music citations.
Analyse, interpret and evaluate your own performance and choreography using correct terminology.
Explain how your performance and choreography help an audience understand the choreographic intent.
Study all six anthology works: Artificial Things, A Linha Curva, Infra, Shadows, Within Her Eyes and Emancipation of Expressionism.
Describe production features: staging, lighting, properties, costume, dancers, aural setting and dance for camera.
Describe the performance environment of each work and the choreographers' approaches from their interviews.
Describe each work's movement content, structure, devices and choreographic intent.
Compare similarities and differences between the six works' defining characteristics.
Explain how choreography, performance and production together shape the audience's understanding.
Explain the purpose of the performance environments in which each work was made and shown.
